title: Nuevo Laredo's Traveling Library Reaches More Than 190 Students
excerpt: Nuevo Laredo's traveling library program brought stories, dramatized readings and interactive activities to more than 190 students at two schools.
content:
Nuevo Laredo's traveling library program has brought books and storytelling to more than 190 students at two schools, according to CML Noticias.

The municipal government's “Biblioteca Itinerante” program, run through the city's arts and culture department and its municipal libraries office, turns classrooms into reading spaces where children discover stories through storytelling, dramatized readings and interactive activities, CML Noticias reported.

At Escuela Primaria “Leyes de Reforma,” in the afternoon shift, 50 students took part in a literary day, with support from school director Mario Garza López and the teaching staff, according to the report.

The program also visited Jardín de Niños “Club de Leones,” in the morning shift, where 140 young children joined activities designed to spark their imagination and bring them closer to books, CML Noticias reported. School director Martha Ruiz Castañón and her team helped run the activities.

Beyond encouraging a love of reading, the program helps students build comprehension, communication and expression skills, according to the report.

Source: CML Noticias, November 15, 2026. Also reported by Reynosa Press.
